title: Why S-Traps Fail: Understanding Trap Siphonage
description: An S-trap occurs when a drain line drops vertically directly after the trap bend without a proper vent break. As water flows through the line, it creates a full siphoning action that pulls the protective water barrier out of the trap seal. Without this liquid barrier, dangerous sewer gases can freely enter the living space. Professional installations replace S-traps with a standard P-trap configuration connected horizontally to a sanitary tee and vent stack. Always verify that the horizontal trap arm length meets local code minimums before making any vertical transitions in the drainage system.

An S-trap occurs when a drain line drops vertically directly after the trap bend without a proper vent break. Without this liquid barrier, dangerous sewer gases can freely enter the living space. Professional installations replace S-traps with a standard P-trap configuration connected horizontally to a sanitary tee and vent stack. Always verify that the horizontal trap arm length meets local code minimums before making any vertical transitions in the drainage system.
